item.statement: Classical molecular dynamics simulations cannot provide quantitatively accurate predictions for multi-element alloys due to the lack of robust intermolecular potentials.
quotes: Classical MD simulations are unable to provide quantitatively accurate predictions of mechanical deformation for these multi-element alloys due to the lack of robust intermolecular potentials.
To extend investigations, we propose a set of intermolecular potential parameters for a quinary Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni alloy
New potentials would enable a classical treatment of such alloys and allow us to examine much larger material domains

item.statement: The study is restricted to high strain rates (~10^10 s^-1) due to computational time constraints, which are orders of magnitude higher than experimentally realizable rates.
quotes: Higher strain rates, ~10^10 s^-1, are chosen to provide predictions within reasonable computational wall-clock times due to length and time scale limitations in MD simulations.
This trend restricts the use of experimentally-realizable high strain rates, ~10^2 s^-1.
Nevertheless, deformation characteristics observed in our investigation are representative of those observed for experimentally-applied high strain rates.

item.statement: The specific mechanisms and extent of thermo-plastic instability under high-strain compression at elevated temperatures require further experimental exploration to fully understand the shear-induced disordering.
item.lever: experimental validation of high-temperature compressive instability
quotes: Large fluctuations under stress, and at higher temperatures, are attributed to the thermo-plastic instability in Al 0.1 CrCoFeNi.
This investigation provides further motivation for the experimental exploration of high-temperature compressive thermo-plastic instability in Al 0.1 CrCoFeNi.
The wide spectrum of thermo-plastic instability fluctuations at elevated temperatures is dissimilar to the instability found in shear bands of alloys under compressive loading conditions.

item.statement: The behavior of the alloy under tensile loading at high strains remains less understood compared to compression, as the clustering-to-ordering transition is absent in tension, leaving the plastic flow mechanism under tension to be further characterized.
quotes: At various temperatures high-strain compression promotes atomistic rearrangements in Al 0.1 CrCoFeNi, resulting in a clustering-to-ordering transition that is absent for tensile loading.
No strain hardening is observed under tensile deformation.
Thus, the transition to ordering state among the different elements of the Al 0.1 CrCoFeNi is possible only for the high compressive strain condition.
